newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean moderate union says Kim's offer not enough.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean moderate union says Kim's offer not enough.

text.p: South Korea's officially-sanctioned trade union body said on Tuesday that President Kim Young-sam's compromise over a controversial labour law fell short of the union's demands and warned of further industrial strife.
But the Federation of Korean Trade Unions welcomed Kim's decision to suspend the execution of arrest warrants outstanding for leaders of a rival umbrella union group outlawed by the government.

"The patched-up solution to reopen debate on the labour law in parliament falls short of the federation's demand to make the vicious labour law completely void and revised," federation leader Park In-sang said in a statement.
"This will not get support from workers," he added.

Park urged the government to involve union representatives for any revision of the labour law and said: "If a revision proceeds as a political compromise excluding management and unions...we will stage a struggle to the end."
President Kim on Tuesday agreed to reopen debate in parliament over the new law in a stunning concession to opposition parties following more than three weeks of strikes.
